author: reek
body: The calculator, moved out of `apps/guios/CalcApp.codex` when the guios shell retired into GopDesk. The arithmetic and the scancode dispatch are that chapter's, unchanged in behaviour; what changed is where the state lives and who owns the loop.

author: reek
body: State was a MutWheel, which is GuiTimer's mutable metadata buffer and one of the chapters retiring. It is a plain 64-byte cell block here, allocated once by `desk-run` and passed in, so entering and leaving the pane allocates nothing.

author: reek
body: This chapter has NO run loop and does no drawing. It answers with a WidgetNode and GopDesk composes that into the chrome's content panel, so the sidebar and taskbar lay out around it and this file never needs to know the sidebar's width. GopScene and GopFiles each compute that offset themselves and their own prose records that the two files "have to agree by hand"; a pane that hands back a tree cannot drift that way.

author: reek
body: Three cells: the accumulator, the number being typed, and the pending operator.

author: reek
body: Typing past the width of the display would run the value off the panel and, at ten digits, past what the accumulator can hold usefully. The digit is dropped rather than wrapping the value.

author: reek
body: Division by zero answers zero rather than faulting. There is nothing behind this desktop to catch a fault, so the calculator must not be the thing that takes the machine down.

author: reek
body: Set-1 make codes. The answer is whether the key changed anything, so the caller repaints on a key that did and does nothing on one that did not: a calculator is event-driven and an idle pane should not be painting.

author: reek
body: The big line is what you are typing, or the accumulator when you are not. The small line under it is the expression so far, so a pending operator is visible rather than remembered.

author: reek
body: The keypad is drawn rather than merely labelled, because the pane is reachable by a click and a user who arrived that way has no reason to know which keys work. The buttons are not hit-tested yet; the labels are the legend for the keyboard.

author: reek
body: The flex is not decoration. A panel is born flexible but a BUTTON is not, so inside a DirRow -- where the main axis is width -- a button with flex 0 and a min width of 0 lays out exactly 0 pixels wide and paints nothing at all. The first capture of this pane showed an empty keypad between two separators, with the tree laid out correctly around it.
